result.title: VIPA: View-Invariant Projector-Based Adversarial Attack
result.summary: Projector-based adversarial attack aims to physically manipulate real-world scenes by projecting adversarial patterns, thereby causing deep image classifiers to produce incorrect predictions. However, existing stealthy projector-based adversarial attack methods model the project-and-capture process in a single and static view, limiting their view-invariant capability and practical applicability in dynamic environments. In this paper, we introduce View-Invariant Projector-Based Adversarial Attack (VIPA), a novel method designed to overcome these limitations by achieving both view-invariant and classifier-agnostic adversarial attacks in the physical world. We first leverage a view-invariant projector-camera system simulation method to model the physical interactions between projected patterns and real-world surfaces. To ensure robustness and stealthiness of the attack across different views, VIPA optimizes adversarial projections by aggregating simulated attack losses from multiple views. This joint optimization across diverse views helps maintain robustness regardless of the viewpoints. Finally, the optimized patterns are physically projected into real-world scenes, where they successfully fool various classifiers from different viewpoints, thereby enabling robust and practical view-invariant adversarial attacks. Our experiments in both targeted and untargeted attacks demonstrate that VIPA consistently achieves higher attack success rates than existing methods, while also enhancing stealthiness and ensuring minimal perceptual degradation across all tested views.

AI.brief_summary: 提出 VIPA，用视角不变的投影-相机仿真建模图案与真实表面的物理交互，并对多视角攻击损失联合优化，得到在物理世界中跨视角、跨分类器都有效的对抗投影。
AI.relevance_reason: 其跨视角扰动与视角不变表示可提供一个压力测试线索：投影造成的物理视觉扰动可能用于核查 LVR 内部视觉状态是否保留视角不变的细节证据，但论文本身针对普通图像分类器，与推理状态机制无直接关联，需进一步核查。
